findings.title: WordPress 7.1.5 Release
findings.summary_md: WordPress published its 7.1.5 security release on November 18, 2026 and recommended immediate updates. The release post lists twenty security-related items, among them an unauthenticated privilege escalation through Template Part block attributes reported by Logan Homolka that WordPress says can lead to remote code execution, plus SQL injection, cross-site scripting and a multisite Administrator-to-Super-Admin escalation. It says automatic background updates will begin for supporting sites, calls 7.1.5 a short-cycle release, and notes that fixes were backported to all branches eligible for security updates, through 4.7.

findings.title: Version 7.1.5 | WordPress.org Documentation
findings.summary_md: The HelpHub page records the November 18, 2026 release and lists the security fixes with their reporters, including the Template Part privilege escalation reported by Logan Homolka and the batched XML-RPC pingback denial of service reported by Giovanni Cintolo. It states that WordPress 7.0 through 6.5 are each affected by all 20 issues, with 6.4 and 6.3 affected by 19, 6.1 and 6.0 by 18, and 5.9 by 17. Fixed branch releases include 7.0.9, 6.9.12, 6.8.13 and 5.9.21, and the page advises updating immediately from `Dashboard > Updates`.

findings.title: An unauthenticated privilege escalation issue via Template Part block attributes that could lead to remote code execution
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory `GHSA-pmp8-6cv8-q323` rates the Template Part block issue High and says the block's theme and slug attributes can make an Administrator's editor send requests to another URL on the same site. An Author can set those attributes in a post, and an unauthenticated attacker can send the Administrator a crafted editor link or redirect them to one; opening it can create an Administrator account for the attacker and lead to code execution through plugin upload. Affected versions run from 5.9.0 through 7.1.4, patched releases run from 5.9.21 through 7.1.5, no CVE ID was assigned at publication, and logansec is credited with the report.

findings.title: An unauthenticated stored cross-site scripting (XSS) issue via shortcode attributes in comments
findings.summary_md: Advisory `GHSA-cr2m-2j4r-3v3x` rates as High a stored cross-site scripting flaw where an unauthenticated visitor posts a comment containing a shortcode whose escaped attribute value decodes into markup after the comment was sanitized. Where a Comments or Latest Comments block was placed in post content, that markup rendered under the post allowlist. Affected versions span 4.7.0 through 7.1.4, the fix is in 7.1.5 and backported to branches back to 4.7, no CVE ID was assigned at publication, and rafiem is credited.

findings.title: An unauthenticated denial of service issue via batched XML-RPC pingbacks
findings.summary_md: Advisory `GHSA-56j2-5mp6-wr3x` describes a Moderate denial of service reachable when an unauthenticated request batches many pingback calls through the XML-RPC `system.multicall` method. Each pingback pauses the request for one second and makes an outbound HTTP request, so a single request can hold a PHP worker for a long time. WordPress fixed it in 7.1.5 and backported the fix to every branch back to 4.7; the advisory lists patched releases including 7.0.9, 6.9.12 and 4.7.40, assigns no CVE ID, and credits giovannicintolo.

findings.title: A multisite privilege escalation issue letting a site Administrator take over a Super Admin account via Customizer menu previews
findings.summary_md: Advisory `GHSA-mwj7-xhp9-7773` says a site Administrator on multisite could replay a Customizer widget hash as the signature for nav menu selective refresh arguments and run a callback of their choice, taking over a Super Admin account. The site must use a classic theme with widgets enabled. The High-severity issue is patched in 7.1.5 and backported to branches back to 4.7, carried no CVE ID at publication, and credits Yuval Miller.
